newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hotel operator Shangri-La 1996 net seen up 21 pct.
newsitem.headline: Hotel operator Shangri-La 1996 net seen up 21 pct.

text.p: Hotel operator Shangri-La Asia Ltd is expected to post 1996 net profit growth of about 21 percent on generally improved business conditions, checked only by a slowdown in China, analysts said on Tuesday.
The hotel arm of Malaysia's Kuok group, which has hotels and investment properties in China, Hong Kong and elsewhere in Asia, is scheduled to announce its 1996 results on Friday.

"Occupancy was high in Hong Kong and Southeast Asia in 1996, so the profit growth was quite good. Only its China business slowed down with lower occupancy because it lost some business travellers," said Dharmala Securities analyst Frederick Fok.
Average analysts' estimates foresee net earnings of HK$1.05 billion (US$135 million) for the year, up 21 percent over 1995, according to the latest edition of the Estimate Directory.
Expectations range from HK$961 million to HK$1.17 billion, representing gains of 12 to 36 percent over 1995, when it posted a 36 percent surge in net profit to HK$860.42 million.
Fok said he estimated the group's average occupancy to be 82 percent in 1996, versus about 78 percent in the previous year.
Shangri-La operates two hotels in Hong Kong, 10 in China, three in the Philippines, one in Indonesia and two in Fiji.
"1996 was one of the best years for Hong Kong hotels," HSBC James Capel analyst Leon Chik said. "All hotels in Hong Kong did well."
He said Shangri-La's Hong Kong properties would contribute 32 percent of its net earnings in 1996.
Fok said its Hong Kong occupancy was about 85 percent in 1996, up from some 81 percent in 1995.
But analysts were less upbeat about the group's hotel operations in China, where it opened three hotels last year.

"It is starting some new hotels in China. They are dragging on the company in the start-up period in the first few years," said Chik, who expected the firm's China hotels and investment properties to make up 52 percent of its 1996 net earnings.
Fok said Shangri-La's China hotel business slowed down amid keen competition, but gave no occupancy estimates.
The hotel owner has said the China market became progressively softer last year.

Increasing airline flight frequency, slower investment in China due to an official austerity plan, and a fall in the number of trade and political delegations visiting the country had reduced the average length of stay, it said.
However, analysts are positive on the firm's 1996 rental income from its China investment properties, for which Fok tipped growth of about 14 percent.
The company saw steady income growth in Asia outside Hong Kong and China, analysts said.
Fok said Shangri-La's occupancy there was about 79 percent in 1996, slightly up from 77 percent in the previous year.
Analysts pointed out there was dilution in the firm's earnings per share due to the issue of 105.72 million new shares last year.
The consensus estimate for earnings per share is HK$0.69 in 1996, up 5.0 percent on 1995, according to the Estimate Directory.
-- Hong Kong Newsroom (852) 2843 6590
